title: fix(storage)!: an unclaimed file is served only within its organization
body:
Fixes #25693

Clause-②: no (narrowing)
Metadata-protocol: none

## What this changes

This PR makes one rule true: **an unclaimed file is served only within its organization**, as every other organization-scoped row is read. An unclaimed file is a private file with neither an attachments scope nor a field owner. It is either an upload that no record has claimed yet, or one whose record let it go.

- **The download doors** (`@objectstack/service-storage`, `storage-routes.ts`, `authorizeDownload`). `GET /api/v1/storage/files/:fileId/url` and `GET /api/v1/storage/files/:fileId` still ask for a signed-in caller first, and answer `401 AUTH_REQUIRED` without one. Then they hand an unclaimed file to the download authorizer, as they already do for every other private file. A `deny` answers `403 FILE_DOWNLOAD_DENIED`, the status and code the doors already give a non-attachment file the caller may not read. Its message names no record. An allowed download keeps the presigned TTL this class has always been minted with. No error code is added.
- **The download authorizer** (`storage-service-plugin.ts`, `buildFileReadAuthorizer` calling the new module-private `isWithinCallerOrganization`). The existing owner shortcut comes first. After it, an unclaimed file is judged in the two places that judge every other organization-scoped row. The first is the organization wall's verdict (`computeTenantLayer0Verdict`, ADR-0131 D8), asked over the caller's resolved context for the posture in force. The second is the driver's tenant term: the row is read by id under the caller's active organization (`tenantId`) and, under `group`, their organization access set. This package writes no organization comparison of its own. The context's organization is the one `resolveRequestExecutionContext` vetted against current membership. A caller with no organization scope under a walled posture is in no organization's reach, as the wall decides for every other row. The door answers that `deny` verdict itself, before the read.

What stays the same:

- The uploader is served their own upload. This is the owner rule every private file already follows.
- The `single` posture serves every signed-in caller, as before.
- `acl: 'public_read'` stays anonymous.
- Attachments-scope and field-owned files keep their parent-derived verdicts.
- An anonymous caller still gets `401 AUTH_REQUIRED`.
- A kernel with no auth service binds no authorizer and still serves these files without a check.

`registerStorageRoutes`' exported `authorizeFileRead` option is now also asked about this class. Its doc says so, and the changeset's BREAKING section covers it.

## Measurement

The card's maintainer word was 「立卡,先实测再修」, so the measurement came first. It ran through the public door on a fresh boot (a real HTTP server under the `isolated` posture, with the organizations runtime loaded) at `b77bb37eb2`, before any edit. Its one-line result is on the card. The detail is with the seat, off GitHub. The same measurement was repeated on the fixed build at `34c018bbad`: the rule holds, and the controls are unchanged. That detail is with the seat too.

## Declarations

- `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`. Under a walled posture the doors serve an unclaimed file to fewer callers, and nothing is widened. The claim carries `Clause-②: no` with no arm. The dispatch asked for the `(narrowing)` arm, and AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3 names that arm for this case, so it is added. The report notes the difference.
- `Metadata-protocol: none`. Nothing a metadata author writes changes.
- One `patch` changeset on `@objectstack/service-storage`, titled `fix(storage)!:`. It carries the BREAKING section (Before / Now / Fix) and the ADR-0087 disposition `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`.
- This PR touches no governed surface. `skip-changeset` is not applied.
- It does not touch `file-reference-lifecycle.ts` (PR #25682 is open there), so the two PRs are file-disjoint.

## Tests (head `34c018bbad`)

- New `packages/services/service-storage/src/unclaimed-file-organization-scope.test.ts`, with 15 tests. It uses a real `ObjectQL` and `SqlDriver` (sqlite `:memory:`) and the real `StorageServicePlugin` booted as it ships, so the door, the session gate, the authorizer and `resolveRequestExecutionContext` are all real. Each case calls both doors, and where a file is served it follows the minted URL to the bytes. The stand-ins are the session read (two test headers), the permission store (`sys_member` fixture rows; empty for every other unregistered object) and the `tenancy` service.
  - `isolated`: refused (`403 FILE_DOWNLOAD_DENIED` at both doors, no URL minted, nothing about the file in the body) to a caller acting in another organization, to a signed-in caller acting in no organization, and to a caller whose session names the file's organization without a membership in it. Served to a colleague in the file's organization and to the uploader. The uploader is also served while acting elsewhere (the owner rule). An anonymous caller gets `401`.
  - Controls under `isolated`: `public_read` is served to anyone, and an attached file keeps `ATTACHMENT_DOWNLOAD_DENIED` for another organization and is served to a colleague.
  - `group`: served to a member of the file's organization who is acting in another of their organizations, and refused to a caller with no membership in it.
  - `single`: served to every signed-in caller whatever organization the session names, and refused (`401`) to an anonymous caller.
- `storage-routes.test.ts`: five existing pins asserted the session-only branch this PR removes. Each was re-judged on its own subject: the unclaimed class now asks the authorizer, its `deny` answers `403 FILE_DOWNLOAD_DENIED`, an allowed download keeps the presigned TTL, and the bare-kernel pin binds no authorizer, as a bare kernel binds none. One route-level pin was added: a denied signed-in caller is refused at both doors and no URL is minted.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/service-storage exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2`: Test Files 63 passed (63), Tests 1147 passed (1147).
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/service-storage typecheck`: exit 0. The test-layer program (`tsconfig.test.json`, checked with `--listFiles`) compiles both test files.
- `eslint --no-inline-config` with the root config over `packages/services/service-storage/src`: exit 0.
- Full dogfood battery (owed for the `(narrowing)` arm): `pnpm --filter @objectstack/dogfood test` under the shared lock, with no shard and no path, on this head. Its counts are in the `os-dev-report` comment on #25693.

## Proof (ablation)

Each leg was mutated through `node scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, which checks on disk that the anchor hit and that the blob changed, then restores and checks the result against the HEAD blob. The subject is this package's source, imported relatively by both suites, so no `dist/` is involved.

- **Leg 1, the door's organization scoping removed for the unclaimed class.** 10 tests went red: all five refusal pins of the new file (three under `isolated`, the refusal-comparison pin, and one under `group`) and the five route-level pins of the unclaimed class. 54 stayed green: every served pin, both controls and the `single` block. Restored: blob `b34c59e7fdcb` equals HEAD's, and `git diff HEAD` is empty.
- **Leg 2, the wall's `deny` exit removed.** Exactly the 2 pins for a caller with no organization scope went red ("acts in no organization", and "names the file's organization without a membership in it"). The other 13 stayed green, so the driver's tenant term alone still refuses another organization. Restored: blob `1b929b2e9d08` equals HEAD's, and `git diff HEAD` is empty.

## Acceptance notes

- **The uploader is served from any organization.** This is the owner shortcut the authorizer already applies to every private file. Should an unclaimed upload be readable by its uploader alone, or by the whole organization? Neither the upload door nor ADR-0104 settles that. This PR keeps the organization scope (plus the uploader) and routes the question to the seat.
- **A platform administrator** reads the unclaimed files of the organization they act in, like any member. The door holds no permission sets, so it grants no wall exemption. The engine makes the same choice for a system read.
- **A file row with no organization** (invalid state on a walled deployment under ADR-0131) is in no organization's reach under a walled posture. Only its uploader is served it.

## Gates

The local subset is the full `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` list for this diff, reconciled with `--ran`. Every family CI runs is read from this PR's check-runs. Both are in the `os-dev-report` comment on #25693.
